Discover Sequential Patterns

Source: R/sequence_patterns.R
sequence_patterns.Rd

Finds the ordered patterns that occur in a set of sequences and reports, for each one, how often it occurs, how many sequences contain it, and its lift. Three pattern types are supported:

"ngram"

Contiguous runs of len states, e.g. A->B->C.

"gapped"

Two states separated by gap positions of any state, e.g. A->*->B (gap 1) or A->**->B (gap 2).

"repeated"

Runs of len identical states, e.g. A->A->A.

A window that contains a missing value is skipped, so a pattern never spans a gap or the end of a sequence.

Usage

sequence_patterns(
  x,
  type = c("ngram", "gapped", "repeated"),
  len = 2:5,
  gap = 1:3,
  min_freq = 2,
  min_support = 0.01,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  contain = NULL,
  pattern = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  adjust = "BH",
  top = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Sequence data, in any form accepted by extract_sequences(): prepared data, a long event log (with action), a wide data frame or character matrix, a netobject, netobject_group or tna model.

type

Pattern type: "ngram" (default), "gapped" or "repeated".

len

Integer vector of pattern lengths for "ngram" and "repeated". Default 2:5.

gap

Integer vector of gap sizes for "gapped". Default 1:3.

min_freq

Minimum number of occurrences. Default 2.

min_support

Minimum share of sequences containing the pattern. Default 0.01.

start, end

Optional character vectors of states. Keep only patterns that begin (start) or end (end) with one of them.

contain

Optional character vector of states. Keep only patterns that include at least one of them.

pattern

Optional template to search for instead of discovering all patterns, e.g. "discuss->*->consensus": each * is one position holding any state (** is two). Every concrete instance is returned as its own row ("discuss->plan->consensus", ...). type, len and gap are then ignored.

group

Optional grouping of the sequences: the name of a column stored with them (a covariate of a wide data frame or long event log, or of a network's metadata), or a vector with one value per sequence. For a netobject_group its own grouping is used when group is NULL. Adds a test of pattern presence by group; see Details. group = "last_obs" uses each sequence's last observed state as its group and removes the states that end some sequence from all sequences (for data whose final state codes the outcome, e.g. an appended "pass"/"fail"; codyna's last_obs).

reference

For two groups, the reference group; the odds ratio is for the other group. Default: the first group in sorted order.

adjust

Multiplicity correction for the group test, passed to p.adjust. Default "BH".

top

Optional number of rows to return (the first top in the output order). Default NULL, all rows.

cols

State columns of a wide data frame; see extract_sequences().

...

Passed to extract_sequences(), e.g. actor, action and time for a long event log.

Value

A data.frame with one row per pattern, ordered by support (then occurrences, then pattern):

pattern

States joined by "->"; * marks a wildcard position.

length

Number of positions the pattern spans.

occurrences

Total number of times it occurs.

proportion

occurrences as a share of all patterns of the same length.

n_sequences

Number of sequences that contain it.

support

n_sequences divided by the number of sequences.

lift

Support relative to independent presence of its states.

With group, also support_<group> (the support within each group); for two groups odds_ratio, or_lower, or_upper; for more, chisq and cramers_v; then p_value and p_adj. Rows are ordered by p_value (then support).

Conditions: nestimate_bad_input for a state name containing "->" or consisting only of asterisks (reserved for wildcards), a missing group column, a group vector of the wrong length, or a group with fewer than two values; warning nestimate_missing_group when sequences with a missing group are dropped.

Details

support is the share of sequences that contain the pattern at least once. lift compares it with the support expected if the states in the pattern appeared in sequences independently: support / prod(state_support), where the support of a state is the share of sequences in which it occurs and wildcard positions are left out. A lift above 1 means the states co-occur in this order more often than independent presence predicts. It does not account for the transition structure: a pattern that the transition probabilities make likely can have a lift above 1.

proportion is computed over all patterns of the same length before min_freq, min_support, start, end and contain are applied, so it does not change with the filters.

Group test

With group, each pattern's presence (in a sequence or not) is cross-tabulated against the group. For two groups, Fisher's exact test gives the p-value, the conditional maximum-likelihood odds ratio of containing the pattern in the non-reference group, and its 95\ confidence interval. A pattern that occurs in one group only has an infinite (or zero) odds ratio, with a finite lower (or upper) limit; a pattern present in every sequence has none (NA). For three or more groups, the Pearson chi-square of the presence-by-group table gives the p-value (G - 1 degrees of freedom), with Cramér's V as the effect size. Unlike a comparison of counts against an equal split, both tests account for unequal group sizes. p-values are adjusted across the returned patterns' family (all patterns passing the filters) with adjust. The rows are then ordered by p_value.

References

Agrawal, R., & Srikant, R. (1995). Mining sequential patterns. Proceedings of the Eleventh International Conference on Data Engineering, 3–14.

Fisher, R. A. (1935). The logic of inductive inference. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, 98(1), 39–82.

See also

pattern_outcome, sequence_compare
